root_cause.text: In raid1_run(), after setup_conf() registers a thread via md_register_thread(), the failure of raid1_set_limits() does not unregister that thread, causing a memory leak of the md_thread structure and associated resources.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "raid1_run() calls setup_conf() which registers a thread via md_register_thread(). If raid1_set_limits() fails, the previously registered thread is not unregistered..." The patch adds `md_unregister_thread(mddev, &conf->thread);` in the error path after the `raid1_set_limits()` call.

This condition incorrectly guards the cleanup: after setup_conf, mddev->private is set, so this check fails, skipping both raid1_free and any thread unregistration. This is a direct cause of the leak.

md/raid1: fix memory leak in raid1_run() if no active rdev

When `raid1_set_limits()` fails or when the array has no act
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 5fbcf76e0dfe68578ffa2a8a691cc44cf586ae35
Author: Zheng Qixing <zhengqixing@huawei.com>
Date:   Sat Feb 15 10:01:37 2025 +0800

    md/raid1: fix memory leak in raid1_run() if no active rdev
    
    When `raid1_set_limits()` fails or when the array has no active
    `rdev`, the allocated memory for `conf` is not properly freed.
    
    Add raid1_free() call to properly free the conf in error path.
    
    Fixes: 799af947ed13 ("md/raid1: don't free conf on raid0_run failure")
    Signed-
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows that in raid1_run(), two error paths now call raid1_free(mddev, conf) when mddev->private is NULL (i.e., conf not yet assigned to mddev->private). This ensures the previously allocated 'conf' (including the md_thread registered via md_register_thread) is properly freed when raid1_set_limits() fails or when there are no active rdevs. Thus, the vulnerability (missing cleanup after thread registration) is fixed in this commit.
